entries.title: Luke 5:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Depart from me, for I am a sinful man - And therefore not worthy to be in thy presence.

entries.title: Luke 5:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: They forsook all and followed him - They had followed him before, John 1:43, but not so as to forsake all. Till now, they wrought at their ordinary calling.

entries.title: Luke 5:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: He withdrew - The expression in the original implies, that he did so frequently.

entries.title: Luke 5:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Sitting by - As being more honourable than the bulk of the congregation, who stood. And the power of the Lord was present to heal them - To heal the sickness of their souls, as well as all bodily diseases.

entries.title: Luke 5:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Not being able to bring him in through the multitude, they went round about by a back passage, and going up the stairs on the outside, they came upon the flat - roofed house, and let him down through the trap door, such as was on the top of most of the Jewish houses: doubtless, with such circumspection as the circumstances plainly required.

entries.title: Luke 5:26
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: We have seen strange things to. day - Sins forgiven, miracles wrought.

entries.title: Luke 5:29
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: And Levi made him a great entertainment - It was necessarily great, because of the great number of guests.

entries.title: Luke 5:33
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Make prayers - Long and solemn. Mt 9:14; Mr 2:18.

entries.title: Luke 5:34
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Can ye make - That is, is it proper to make men fast and mourn, during a festival solemnity?

entries.title: Luke 5:36
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: He spake also a parable - Taken from clothes and wine; therefore peculiarly proper at a feast.

entries.title: Luke 5:39
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: And no man having drunk old wine - And beside, men are not wont to be immediately freed from old prejudices.
